rule.question: Was the registrant bearing this ticker today the company the filing named then?
rule.derived_from: SEC submissions JSON: formerNames with from/to windows, and filings.files[] filingFrom/filingTo bounds, which give the full filing history in ONE request per registrant.
rule.decidable_part: A registrant whose first filing postdates the disclosure, or whose last filing predates it, cannot be the company named. Both are lineage breaks.
rule.judgement_part: A registrant filing at the time under a different name may be a subsidiary, a brand, or the wrong company. Reported for review, never decided here.
rule.what_continuous_does_not_mean: It removes one way of being wrong. A merger that preserved both the name and the registrant would pass and still be the wrong peer -- which is how Caremark RX and OfficeMax were caught, on the merits rather than by this test.
rule.fails_closed: Every gap in the record yields UNKNOWN, never a pass. Today's name is never assumed to have been in force before the former-name windows close.
rule.promotes_nothing: No row is curated, no edge is written, and no candidate is cleared for use. The display gate is untouched.

what_this_is: Whether each ticker-resolved candidate's registrant was the company its anchor's filing actually named.
what_this_is_not: Curation. No row is promoted, no edge is written, and a CONTINUOUS verdict clears one specific error, not the relationship.
what_changed_from_v1: Adds the live control. v1's verdicts are unchanged and all seven were CONTINUOUS, which is precisely when a check needs to be shown capable of failing.

control.detail: the registrant's first filing is 2022-04-13, AFTER the 2006-02-08 filing that named 'Ingram Micro'. It cannot be the company that disclosure named.
control.why_this_control_exists: Every real candidate returned CONTINUOUS. A check that has never been observed to fire is not known to work, so the audit re-runs the case that motivated it and refuses if that case does not break.
